name: Krisp
tagline: Real-time AI noise cancellation and meeting voice enhancement

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Core/Pro is listed at $16/user/month monthly and $8/user/month annually.

verdictSummary: You can build post-processing and maybe route audio through open models, but real-time low-latency virtual-device noise cancellation is not a one-sitting web app.
coreLoopDIY: Use an open noise-suppression model as a virtual microphone or post-process recordings before sending them to calls or files.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because audio cleanup must be instant and invisible during real calls.

priorArt.name: RNNoise
priorArt.desc: Open-source recurrent noise suppression model; useful but not a full Krisp replacement.

notes: Interesting because AI model availability does not remove OS/audio-driver product complexity.
prompt:
Build me a personal replacement for Krisp (Real-time AI noise cancellation and meeting voice enhancement). Requirements:

- Core loop: Use an open noise-suppression model as a virtual microphone or post-process recordings before sending them to calls or files.
- Needs: audio DSP library.
- Needs: OS-level virtual audio device.
- Needs: model/runtime optimized for low latency.
- Needs: macOS/Windows audio permissions.
- Keep it personal-scale: no accounts, no telemetry, secrets in .env, SQLite or
  flat files for storage. Local-first wherever possible.
- Clean minimal UI where one is needed; CLI is fine where one is not.
- Include a README with setup steps, required keys, and any OS permissions.

Honest scope: this covers the core loop only. You will not get: low-latency virtual microphone; polished app switching; model quality.
